strings.ice.3f69475c: The City of Mansfield runs Clear Fork Reservoir as a water supply lake and posts no ice report. No public gauge posts the level. Call the park police before going out on the ice.
strings.ice.4a0bda2f: ODNR posts no ice report for Lake Logan, and the lake is drawn down for winter (ODNR). No public gauge posts the level. Call the park office before going out on the ice.
strings.ice.4e0a960b: The US Army Corps of Engineers manages Delaware Lake’s water level for flood control, and ODNR lists a 5 ft winter drawdown. Call the state park office before going out on the ice.
strings.ice.4e284169: Columbus runs Hoover for drinking water, and the city describes it as “subject to significant water level fluctuation.” Reservoir rules are in Columbus City Code Chapters 919 and 921. Check them before going out on the ice.
strings.ice.4f15b2ac: ODNR names Buckeye Lake one of the best places for saugeye through the ice, because it is shallow and generally freezes quickly. Ice that forms fast is still not safe ice. Call the state park office before going out.
strings.ice.5e29e5c0: ODNR posts no ice report for West Branch Reservoir. USGS posts the lake level. Call the park office before going out on the ice.
strings.ice.67411689: ODNR’s thickness guidelines are minimums for new, clear, solid ice only, and it says many things other than thickness can make ice unsafe. Read them there; this site doesn’t repeat them as a go or no go.
strings.ice.6ff7e87a: The US Army Corps of Engineers manages Alum Creek’s water level. Call the state park office before going out on the ice.
strings.ice.724d41fd: Tell someone exactly where you are going, where you will park and when you will be back.

strings.ice.8433c3c6: No public gauge posts Madison Lake’s level, and ODNR posts no ice report for it. Madison Lake is run from the Deer Creek State Park office; call before going out on the ice.

strings.ice.a9f2dff5: ODNR: “In Ohio, anglers can have up to six tip-ups going at one time and each must be labeled with the owner’s name and address.” Hole size, shelters and the rest are in the current Ohio fishing regulations. Verify them before you go.
